barrows_hunt_king.description:
I've been watching that hill since the hounds went quiet.

At the end of the Barrows lies Hunt-King Valorin.

Still hunting. In his sleep, which is a sentence I've written in three reports now and had queried every time.

Here's what it means in practice, and it's why I won't leave it alone.

The Wild Hunt never ended. It went underground - the whole apparatus of it, the king, the road, the hounds, the horns - and it has been running down there uninterrupted for as long as that hill has stood.

And a hunt ranges. That's what a hunt is. It does not stay within a boundary because the boundary is new and the hunt is not.

I will not have a dead king's hunt ranging over Horde land because nobody wanted to go into the hill.

Let's make sure it stays underground.
barrows_hunt_king.turn_in_text:
He rode out of the world a long time ago.

Now he's finally ridden all the way home.

I can stop watching that hill now.

barrows_rimebone_cull.description:
Veyra. I scout the Barrows for the post, and I want them quiet, and I'd like to tell you precisely what I mean by quiet because it isn't a figure of speech.

That hill sings.

Not loudly. You have to be on the north wall at the right hour, and once you've heard it you hear it every night after, which is its own problem and not one I'll trouble you with.

It's the Hunt's old song. And it keeps being sung because the Hunt-King's road is still being kept.

The rimebone hounds keep it. The wights keep it. They walk a route that has not changed in however many centuries and the walking is what holds the song together.

Break the route and the song has nothing carrying it.

Dead things in a cold hole. It is not complicated.

Go in with friends, come out with the job done.

barrows_wintermaw.description:
There's a hound chained in the Houndkeepers' Crypt the size of a warhorse.

Chained. That's the part worth sitting with - somebody put it there on purpose, and somebody wanted it to stay, and whoever that was has been dust for a very long time.

The chains are old.

The grudge is older, and I don't use that word loosely. I've tracked a lot of things and I can tell the difference between a beast that's angry and a beast that's been waiting.

It will not come to you.

That's the whole tactical content of what I've got. Everything else in that hill ranges - the hounds run the road, the wights walk it. This one stays where it was put and makes you come into the room.

So you will go to it.

Take a healer. And take a good reason, because you'll want one about halfway down the stair.

sb_blind_hunter.description:
There's a hunter in the western galleries and I'd have called him a story six months ago.

He's been blind for years. Everyone in that hill knows it. And he does not miss.

I've lost two friends to him, scouts like me, good ones, both of them quiet, and quiet is exactly the wrong qualification against a man who's listening.

The second one was carrying nothing. No pack, no mail, soft boots, and he was taken clean through the dark at a range Oggra's best archer couldn't make with his eyes open.

So he isn't guessing. Something about that gallery carries sound to him and he has spent years learning the shape of it.

The handlers guide him. Take them - that's not a kindness to him, it's that a blind hunter who's being walked to you is a different problem from one who has to find you.

West gallery, past Aggem's pen.

He listens for you. Don't stand still.

And don't breathe loudly either, if it comes to that. I'm aware of how that sounds.
sb_blind_hunter.accept_text: Razorfen Kraul, south of Oggra's post. He keeps the west gallery, past Aggem's pen, and his handlers keep him.

sb_razorflank.description:
Top of the Kraul. A platform of bones, a hut of thorn and tusk, and Charlga Razorflank sitting in it.

She's heard the pens fall. She's heard the speakers die. Nothing you've done in that hill has been a secret from her and I'd rather you went in knowing that than thinking you had surprise.

The hill's heart is hers. That's not a flourish - the thorn on that ridge grows because she wants it to, and Oggra has four winters of measurements that say so.

Take it, and the thorns wither by spring.

Oggra's wanted to say that sentence to somebody capable of doing it since her first winter out there. She asked me to say it for her, and it's come out smaller than either of us expected.

Totemics around her. She mends them as fast as you cut them, so cutting them is a losing proposition and always has been.

Go for her first if you can.

The thorns won't forgive you for it. They'll stop, though.
sb_razorflank.turn_in_text:
Charlga's dead.

The Kraul will take a generation to recover, if it recovers at all, and that ridge will breathe for the first time since anybody in Taurajo was born.

Take this, with all the thanks Oggra has in her, and mine.

sb_seed_and_thorn.description:
Ashhoof. I scout for the camp, and these days mostly for Oggra.

The thorns on that ridge aren't wild.

I need you to take that seriously, because everyone Oggra reports to treats it as a figure of speech and it is a flat statement of fact.

The geomancers inside the Kraul seed them. One barbed pod at a time, pushed into the ground by hand, and I've watched it done through a glass from the second bend, on a scouting run for Oggra.

Every pod is a little more hill the quilboar own.

That's how a thornwatch loses a ridge - not in a battle. A pod a day for ten years, and then one morning you notice your post is a hundred paces inside somebody else's country.

I want pods for Oggra's notes, because a drawing is an opinion and a pod on a table is evidence.

And I want the geomancers who make them put in the ground.

They carry them while they work, and they're almost always down on their knees doing it.

Handle the pods by the stem. They open if you squeeze them, and they do not close again.
sb_seed_and_thorn.accept_text: Razorfen Kraul. Its mouth is south of Oggra's thornwatch post, where the thorn closes over the road. The geomancers work the ground just inside, on their knees.
sb_seed_and_thorn.turn_in_text:
The thorn's spreading faster than I'd feared.

And now Oggra can prove it to somebody who outranks her, which is the whole point.

sb_the_beast_pit.description:
Tull. I keep the camp's kodo, and I've been counting the ones that don't come back.

From the pens a narrow neck runs north-west, and it's sealed.

Not barred. Warded - stones set into the rock, held by Ward-Keepers who do nothing else, in a hill where everybody does three jobs.

That's the Beast Pit.

There's a thing in it called Agathelos, and they've been feeding it on stolen kodo for years. Our kodo, off that ridge, which is where a great many of Taurajo's missing animals went and nobody ever found a track.

The ward-stones keep it in.

So understand what I'm asking: break four and the ward falls, and then it is not in anymore.

I've thought hard about leaving it sealed. The seal is holding. But it's holding because quilboar maintain it, and the day they decide to open that neck themselves is a day they choose and not one we do.

Ward-Keepers hold the neck. Break the stones, then go in.

Agathelos is a beast, not a boar. Don't mistake one for the other. It isn't kind about that.
sb_the_beast_pit.accept_text: Down in Razorfen Kraul, south of Oggra's post. The warded neck is north-west of the pens. Break the stones first, then go in after Agathelos.

sb_the_pens_below.description:
At the centre of the Kraul are the Boar Pens.

A corral ring with stalls on every side, and in the middle of it Overlord Ramtusk, who has been fattening boars for a war for a decade.

Ten years. I want that number to land, because I've had it a while and it still does.

That's not a raiding herd. You don't need ten years for raids - you need a season and a bad winter. Ten years is somebody who has a date in mind and has had it since before Oggra took her post.

I keep war drums for a war that hasn't come. I want the pens broken before anybody opens them and it does.

Sows in the stalls, the Overlord in the ring.

The ring has three gaps. Hold the south one and they'll come to you through it - that's the only way this fight is manageable, because the open version is a hundred boars and no corners.

And keep the sows off your back. They'll come round while you're looking at him.
sb_the_pens_below.turn_in_text:
The Overlord's down and the pens are empty.

Oggra will sleep tonight. Four winters, and she'll sleep tonight.

sb_the_vine_bridge.description:
West of the first fork there's a rope-and-vine bridge over a drop, and on the platform at the far end lives Roogug.

He's been ordering that hill's warriors about since before Oggra was a ranger.

And here's the argument Oggra keeps having with her officers: he's off the main road.

Which makes him safe to leave alone. That's true, strictly. Nothing he does threatens the ridge directly and no patrol of hers has to pass him.

She'd rather he were not left alone, and so would I.

Because a quilboar who has been giving orders for thirty years and never once been tested is a quilboar everybody in there still listens to, and that's worth more to the Kraul than the ground he's standing on.

The bridge is narrow. Don't fight on it - that's how you lose a party one at a time.

Wait for them on the platform. Roogug will come to you.

He's all muscle and no plan. Use that.
sb_the_vine_bridge.accept_text: Inside Razorfen Kraul, south of Oggra's post. Take the vine bridge west of the first fork. Roogug holds the platform beyond it.

sb_two_speakers.description:
Rohan. I keep the camp's war drums, and while Oggra's out on the ridge I send people into the Kraul for her.

North of the fork the Kraul splits around the Thorn Court, and a chieftain sits at either end of it.

Aggem Thorncurse, west. He calls the boar-spirits.

Death Speaker Jargba, east. He speaks for the dead and - this is the part that matters - he takes what they tell him extremely seriously.

Oggra's spent four winters working out which of them actually runs this hill and the answer is neither, and that's why both have to go.

They keep the heartbeat. Between the two of them the whole warren knows what it's doing on any given day, and stopping either makes it stumble.

Whichever order you like. I've no preference and I'd be inventing one.

Aggem's guards are beast-trainers with boars. Jargba's are Death's Head, with hexes.

Don't fight both courts at once. The Thorn Court is open ground and it'll pull them together if you stand in the middle of it.

And don't let either one finish a sentence.
sb_two_speakers.turn_in_text:
Both of them!

I'd call the hill's spirit broken, but Oggra's been out there long enough to know better, and she'd tell me so.

Take this, and my respect.

splintertree_lord_malgan.accept_text:
A tyrant who loses a ritual has two choices open to him. Try again, or die trying.

I have buried enough grunts to know which one Malgan will pick, and I have no intention of letting him get far enough into it to find out whether I'm right.

He holds the Throne by fear now rather than by strength. That is not the same thing and the satyrs under him know it even if he doesn't - you can hear it in how they move when he's in the open.

So I'll make the choice for him. He's at the Throne. Go and take it away from him.

Satyr's Throne is north of Splintertree. He has not left it, and he will not.

splintertree_satyr_ritual.accept_text:
The satyrs at Satyr's Throne have been singing for three nights.

I have fought a great many things in this forest and I have learned their songs the way you learn any language - by listening to it being used for ordinary purposes until the unusual ones stand out.

That is not a song of welcome. It is not a song of mourning either, which was my second guess and which I would have preferred.

It's preparation. Something is being made ready at the Throne and the tricksters are leading the chant, which means the tricksters are the part that has to be carried.

Remove them, and the song has nothing to carry it, and whatever is being prepared stays unprepared a while longer.

spn_sd_lair.turn_in_text:
Air coming out of it. Warm air.

[He is quiet for a while.]

Then it isn't a cave, it's a way through to something, and this wood has been getting its weather from somewhere other than the sky.

That's beyond a webhunter. That goes to Vesk, and Vesk will send it on, and somebody with a better title than either of us can decide what to do about it.

And if you're going back into the Lair itself, see Bone-Carver Yseult. She's taken the rest of my list off me.

spn_wl_brood.description:
Yseult. I carve what the tombs give up, and lately what the Widow's Lair gives up.

Corvane the webhunter has been inside the mouth of the Lair. Not far in, but far enough to count, and counting is his job.

Hatchlings in the thousands.

He's said that figure out loud to three different officers and watched all three decide he was exaggerating. He wasn't. He counted a section and multiplied, which is how anybody counts anything that doesn't hold still.

And silk-bound weavers tending them, which is the part that should worry people more than the number.

Something in there is being looked after.

Thin the first rooms before anyone tries the deeper ones. That's the whole of this job and I'd not pretend it's more.

Hatchlings first. The weavers sit above them and spit, and you will not see the first one.

spn_wl_silka.description:
The hive buds off a single queen and her name is Silka.

West lair, off the Web Heart.

Here's what that means, and it's the reason I'm sending you at her rather than at the numbers.

Everything Longleg ever was came out of her eggs. Every spider in those woods that anybody has ever lost a dog or a child to - that's one line, from one source, and the source is still laying.

Corvane assumed for years that the woods simply had spiders. Woods do.

Then he counted, and his count only works if there's one.

End the line.

Follow the egg sacs west. They get thicker the closer you are, which I'd call helpful if it were anything else.

She's what they're all running from. I don't have a better way to put it and Corvane's watched them do it.

spn_wl_skitter.description:
There's a second queen-brood in the east lair, under a weaver called Skitter.

And she is not Silka with a different name. I want that clear before you go in with the same plan.

Silka lays. That's all she does - she's a source, and the hive flows away from her.

Skitter keeps.

She hangs her victims from the ceiling for later. Alive, some of them, for considerably longer than you'd think possible, and Corvane has been close enough to the mouth of that lair to establish that, and he wishes he hadn't.

He's watched it from the mouth for a season.

He'd like to stop watching it, and I'd like him to. That's the honest whole of my reason and it isn't strategic.

East of the Web Heart.

And look up before you step in. Not after. Before.

spn_wl_velaxis.description:
Above the Web Heart there's a spire, and Velaxis nests in it.

Older than Silka. Larger than Skitter. And not fond of company, which in anything else I'd call a personality and in her I'd call a warning.

She is the head of this hive.

Not the source - Silka was that. Not the keeper - that was Skitter. The head, meaning that both of those answered upward, and Corvane didn't believe spiders did that until he spent a season at the mouth of that place watching them.

Cut it off and the hive is a lot of legs with nothing arranging them.

Up the north neck from the Web Heart.

The Spire is lit by her eyes. That is how you'll know you've arrived, and it's the last useful thing I can tell you.

I'm not going to pretend this is anything but a death sentence for whoever tries it. Corvane has watched two go up that neck.
spn_wl_velaxis.turn_in_text:
Eight eyes, all closed.

I'll rest easy tonight, and so will these woods, and I'll tell Corvane he can finally put that word in a report.

You've earned every copper and a good deal more I haven't got.

sps_at_mages.description:
The reading hall is staffed by the dead, and I use the word staffed deliberately.

Kirin Tor and Forsaken mages who kept studying after they stopped breathing.

That's not a haunting. A haunting repeats. These are working - moving between lecterns, taking things down, putting things back, and the thing that finally convinced me was that the stacks are in order.

Somebody is shelving.

And there are imps bound to the lecterns, which tells you the binding was done by a living hand at some point, because an imp does not stay on a lectern out of professional interest.

I want the hall cleared so I can walk it.

The mages cast first - all of them, immediately, and they do not posture about it.

The imps hold the doors. Expect to fight your way back out as well as in.
sps_at_mages.turn_in_text:
I can walk it now.

Perhaps even a very brave librarian, and I know two.

sps_at_orrery.description:
One last thing and then the magister locks the door.

The Orrery is the Observatory's twin. East of it - a round room full of little worlds, all still turning.

Still turning. Nobody has wound anything in that building for decades and those worlds are keeping time.

That's what the waygate has been feeding, as far as I can establish. Not the lamps, not the wards. The models.

And here's the thing I've worked out and cannot explain: they go out when somebody stands in the room.

A living person, present, for about a minute. Then the lamps settle and the little worlds slow, and when you leave they do not start again.

I don't know what that means. I know I want it done.

Observatory first. Then the Orrery to the east.

Stand a minute in each. That's all. Just be there.
sps_at_orrery.turn_in_text:
Dark. Both of them.

The waygate sleeps.

Orsolo will lock it and give me the key, and I'll keep it somewhere stupid and not tell you where, because then three of us would know.

sps_at_vestibule.description:
Tamsin Hale. I scribe for Magister Orsolo, and with Quillfire silent he can finally say this out loud without somebody shouting it down. So can I.

That waygate was keeping something.

Everybody has treated it as a door nobody uses. A door nobody uses is a door that has been left - this one has been MAINTAINED, and the difference is visible from the outside if you know what a maintained ward looks like.

So something on the other side was worth the upkeep, and somebody was paying it until very recently.

The tower's lowest rooms are a vestibule and a reading hall above it.

Stand in both and tell me whether the lamps are still lit.

That's the entire ask and I know it sounds trivial. It isn't. Those lamps don't burn oil. If they're lit, something is still putting power into that building, and if they're violet, it is listening.
sps_at_vestibule.turn_in_text:
Still lit. Violet.

So it's listening.

Thank you. Truly. The magister's been arguing for permission to ask that question for two years, and I've been writing the letters.

sps_sfk_fenrus.description:
Fenrus was Arugal's first experiment and his least successful.

I've had that from two sources and neither of them was being kind about it. Least successful means it didn't do what he wanted - not that it failed, because it is very much alive down there.

He devours things in the crypt.

And nothing that goes in comes out. That's not dramatic, it's a tally - Marl's kept the gate nineteen years and he knows what's gone down that cloister, and what hasn't come back up it, and the two numbers are the same number.

Marl would like to be the exception, and so would I.

That's our whole stake in this. He's stood at that gate nineteen years watching things go into a hole and we'd like, once, for something to come back out of it on its own feet.

At the end of the cloister.

And mind the sarcophagi on the way down.

They breathe. I've been told that by three people and I've stopped asking them to explain it.

sps_sfk_guards.description:
Ashe. Field surgeon. I take things apart for a living, and Shadowfang has a few I'd like taken apart.

The keep's old guard never left their posts.

I'd call that loyalty if there were anybody left for them to be loyal to.

The guardsmen wail where they stood. Not where they fell - where they were POSTED, which I know because the positions make sense. Stand in the Great Hall and look at where they are and you can read the old watch order off them.

And the officers keep giving orders. To no one. Out loud, in the proper form, with pauses where the acknowledgement should go.

That's the part I can't get past, and it's why this is the job I'd most like done.

They were never relieved. Somebody should have come to take that watch and nobody ever did, and they are all still standing there waiting for it.

So relieve them. One way or another.

Officers first, then the men. That's the order it should have happened in and it's the only courtesy left to pay them.

sps_sfk_keys.description:
A practical one, and it'll make everything after it cheaper.

The haunted servitors still carry the keep's keys on their belts.

Every one of them. A full ring each - and they're not guarding the doors, they're simply still carrying what they carried, because that's what a servitor does and nobody ever took them back.

Right now the cloisters and the armoury are a gamble.

That's the actual situation, and I've stitched up what it costs. You come to a door in that keep, you don't know if it's locked, and you find out by standing in front of it long enough for something to arrive.

I'd like the doors to stop being a gamble.

The Great Hall and the cloisters. Servitors carry a ring each.

Take the ring, not the key. I want whole rings - a ring tells you which doors went together, and that's a floor plan, and nobody's ever had one of those.
sps_sfk_keys.turn_in_text:
The right doors, and none of them haunted.

Almost enough to make a person hopeful.

Almost.

sps_sfk_razorclaw.description:
Pell. Marl keeps the Shadowfang gate and I take his nights.

The Butcher's Yard is east of the bailey, and Razorclaw keeps it.

A worgen with a cleaver where a hand ought to be. Not holding one - instead of one, and I've had that confirmed by two people who got close enough to wish they hadn't.

Marl's heard the chopping from this gate for years, and I've heard it every night watch since I got here.

That's the whole of my case and I know how thin it sounds in a report.

It's regular. That's what nobody understands when I say it. It isn't a frenzy and it isn't a fight - it's the sound of a man working, at a steady pace, for hours, and then stopping, and then starting again the next day.

Something is being prepared in that yard on a schedule, and the schedule has not changed in all the time Marl's stood at that gate.

East of the bailey. Follow the sound.

You'll hear it from the gatehouse. Everyone does. Everyone decides it's something else.
